title: Redwood x HelioCloud marketplace & reference architecture tech sync
summary: Partner technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for Redwood Private on HelioCloud marketplace, billing/integration flow, and joint solution artifacts. Discussed security checklist (SOC2/KMS/SSO), packaging (helm, AMI/container), and pilot plan. Agreed on next steps: share draft RA, marketplace checklist, pricing spreadsheet, and schedule security deep-dive.
topics: marketplace listing metadata and billing model
security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you all making time. We got 42 minutes on the calendar, so we'll try to cover marketplace listing, reference architecture, and the joint solution artifacts. Uh Samir, do you want to kick us off on the tech side?
[00:26] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Yeah sure, hey Priya, Tomas, Lina. Quick background: Redwood's looking to list a Dedicated & Private offering on HelioCloud marketplace, with both hosted SaaS purchase and a private/VPC deployment tile. Technical ask is around the reference arch, packaging options (helm chart vs AMI), and the billing integration - marketplace subscription vs direct invoicing.
[00:52] Priya Reddy (HelioCloud PM): Thanks, Samir. From marketplace side we need the listing metadata, icons, pricing SKUs, and also a verified reference architecture doc so we can publish the solution. We also need to confirm what components run in customer VPC vs Helio managed infra.
[01:15] Tomás Alvarez (HelioCloud Cloud Architect): Quick Q: for the private deployment, do you have an air-gapped on-prem package or is it VPC-only? That affects how we show options in the listing.
[01:26] Maya Lopez (Redwood Solutions Eng): We support VPC peering and an on-prem bundle. The on-prem is a package with container images + helm charts and optional HSM/KMS integrations for customers requiring air-gap. We should clarify in the RA which artifacts are required for each mode.
[01:48] Lina Park (HelioCloud Security): From security I'm going to need SOC2 type 2 attestation, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, and SSO/SAML integration patterns. Also audit logging endpoints.
[02:05] Samir: Yeah, we can provide SOC2 report and KMS integration notes. We have two patterns: 1) Redwood-managed keys (for hosted) and 2) customer-managed KMS (for private/VPC). We should document the KMS key rotation expectations.
[02:28] Evan Brooks (HelioCloud DevRel): Great. On the marketplace UI side, we also prefer to have a 1-click deploy for VPC tile if possible, but we know that's sometimes misleading; we can show an assisted deploy option.
[02:44] Alex: Let's walk through an initial RA outline. Samir, you said helm and AMI. Can you sketch the components and network boundaries?
[02:58] Samir: Sure. Top-level: control plane (Redwood) and data plane (customer). For Dedicated we can run data plane on Helio infra as a managed cluster; for Private it's deployed into customer VPC. Components: model serving nodes (GPU), inference router, KV cache, S3-compatible storage for artifacts, and observability agents that send metrics to Redwood console. We should call out persistent storage requirements and EBS sizing for the GPU nodes.
[03:30] Tomás: Do you require direct peering, or can you operate via private link? We prefer PrivateLink for security isolation.
[03:38] Maya: PrivateLink is supported; we also have an option for VPC peering if the customer prefers. We'll note both with pros/cons in RA.
[03:51] Priya: Marketplace listing needs screenshots, a short blurb, bullets for capabilities, and a quickstart. Do you have a one-page architecture diagram we can use?
[04:03] Alex: We can supply a high-level diagram and a more detailed reference architecture PDF. We'll also include a checklist for Helio's marketplace review.
[04:12] Lina: On telemetry, can customers opt out of sending token-level telemetry? We need to be clear for privacy regs.
[04:21] Samir: Yes, there's an opt-out and we can redact token content. We send anonymized metrics by default and have a strict PII redaction policy. That will be in the security appendix.
[04:41] [Speaker 3 - maybe customer]: Uh yeah, just to add, for billing, Helio wants to support billing via marketplace subscription for hosted, and via usage-metered charges for dedicated. How does Redwood expose usage metrics?
[04:55] Maya: We expose per-route/per-model token counts, latency, and token billing reports. For marketplace metering we can push usage files or integrate with Helio's billing API. We'll need to align on schema and interval (hourly vs daily).
[05:17] Priya: Schema details please, send sample CSV or API contract.
[05:22] Alex: Action item, Alex to send usage export schema and sample file.
[05:28] Samir: Another technical note: for the private deployment, KV cache warming and cold-start behavior matter. We should document how the model cold-start impacts latency, and recommended batch sizes. Also mention quantization profiles for cost-savings.
[05:49] Tomás: Are there prebuilt images for GPU types (A100/V100) or do we provide a container that customers build themselves?
[05:58] Maya: We publish optimized container images for common instance types (A100, H100, etc.) and also provide build instructions. For marketplace we can include an image with tags per architecture.
[06:12] Lina: Regarding encryption in transit, do you support mTLS between Redwood control plane and customer data plane?
[06:19] Samir: Yes, mTLS and mutual auth is supported; we'll include the certificate rotation guidance. For HSM/KMS integration we have verified patterns with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault, but GCP CMEK notes are slightly different.
[06:40] Evan: Small nit: Marketplace listing needs to indicate supported regions. Which regions do you guarantee for dedicated?
[06:47] Alex: For the listing we'll state supported regions and call out expected latency SLOs per region. For Dedicated customers, region availability depends on Helio marketplace capacity; we'll show recommended regions and fallback policies.
[07:06] Priya: For the reference arch doc, Helio needs an operations runbook: install steps, upgrade process, rollback process. Can Redwood provide an operator's playbook?
[07:16] Maya: Yes, we have an ops playbook and an upgrade matrix (minor/major upgrades). We'll include helm upgrade commands and rollbacks and example canary rollout configs.
[07:32] [00:07:32] Speaker 2 (maybe Redwood): There's also a testing harness we can share to run perf tests on Helio infra as part of the validation.
[07:40] Tomás: That would be helpful. We can run a compatibility test against our GPU instance catalog.
[07:47] Samir: We'll provide a perf harness and a config for concurrency profiles. We should also coordinate on test data and synthetic prompts to avoid PII.
[08:05] Priya: On joint solutions / GTM, Helio wants joint collateral: reference arch, quickstart, and a demo script. Is Redwood OK with co-branded collateral?
[08:14] Alex: Absolutely, co-branded collateral is fine. We'll share a draft case study template as well.
[08:22] Lina: Security review: we'll need to run Helio's security questionnaire and possibly an architecture deep-dive. When can we schedule that?
[08:31] Alex: Suggest next week for a security deep-dive with Lina and Redwood security lead. We'll propose two time slots.
[08:42] Evan: Marketplace legal requires indemnification language; Priya, you'll handle that with legal but Redwood should provide standard marketplace terms.
[08:51] Priya: Yep, I'll loop in legal.
[08:56] Samir: Back to packaging: for the marketplace deployable, Helio often expects a one-click CloudFormation or Terraform template. We can provide Terraform module for the VPC deployment and a helm chart for the app stack.
[09:13] Tomás: Terraform+helm is our preferred pattern. Also we want to show resource estimates (vCPU, memory, GPU, storage) so customers can see cost calc.
[09:24] Maya: We'll include recommended instance types and a cost estimator snippet for the listing.
[09:31] [00:09:31] Speaker 4 (customer): A quick ops question: how do upgrades impact model state / KV cache?
[09:38] Samir: Good question - we persist checkpoints to S3 compatible storage. KV cache is ephemeral and warms up; we'll document checkpointing frequency and recommended warm-up procedures.
[09:51] Priya: For the listing we need a short video (90s) demo. Can Redwood produce a screen capture of the deploy flow and console?
[09:59] Alex: Yes, Redwood marketing can produce a short 90s video. Action: Alex to connect Priya with marketing.
[10:07] Lina: On audit logs, does Redwood provide customer-facing logs for inference requests and admin actions? We need retention policy details.
[10:15] Maya: We can stream audit logs to customer SIEM via syslog or Kinesis; retention is configurable up to X months (we'll fill exact value in RA).
[10:28] Tomás: Any special networking ports required? Need to include in our network policy doc.
[10:34] Samir: We'll provide a port list: gRPC 443, metrics 9090 (prometheus), and internal control-plane ports; will include in the RA.
[10:46] Evan: For the marketplace listing, what's the expected lead time from submission to publish?
[10:53] Priya: Typically 2-3 weeks once we have all artifacts and security review passes.
[10:58] Alex: That timeline works. Let's set a target: submit by May 14 so publish could be early June.
[11:07] [00:11:07] Speaker 1 (Redwood): Recap we should make clear: artifacts needed are RA PDF, one-page diagram, ops playbook, helm chart/Terraform module, marketplace screenshots and video, pricing SKUs, and security docs.
[11:22] Priya: Also a contact for support escalation during marketplace deploy.
[11:28] Alex: We'll nominate a tech contact and an AE for post-purchase onboarding.
[11:33] Samir: Security deep-dive: Lina requested key rotation docs and mTLS configuration examples. We'll prepare that.
[11:45] Tomás: For performance validation, we'll need a test account or eager sandbox on Helio where Redwood can deploy the tile and run perf harness. Can Helio provide ephemeral infra for the pilot?
[11:58] Priya: Yes, we can provision a sandbox project. Action: Priya to create a sandbox project and invite Redwood engineers.
[12:10] Alex: Great. On billing metering schema, Redwood will provide a CSV example of usage exports and an API contract for real-time metering.
[12:20] Maya: Also note any differences for hosted vs dedicated (meter granularity).
[12:27] Evan: For the marketplace page, we like to include customer logos and a short testimonial; do you have any early customers we can quote?
[12:35] Alex: We have pilot customer AcmeAI willing to be a reference, I'll check marketing clearance.
[12:42] Priya: Perfect. So next steps and owners?
[12:46] Alex: I'll call them out.
[12:50] [00:12:50] --- QUICK ACTION ITEMS ---
[12:52] Alex Chen - Share marketplace checklist, usage export schema, and connect marketing to Priya - Due 2027-05-07
[12:58] Priya Reddy - Provision Helio sandbox project and invite Redwood engineers - Due 2027-05-06
[13:05] Samir Patel - Provide perf harness, port list, and KMS integration notes - Due 2027-05-09
[13:12] Maya Lopez - Deliver ops playbook and helm chart repo link - Due 2027-05-10
[13:18] Lina Park - Schedule security deep-dive and send questionnaire - Due 2027-05-08
[13:24] Alex Chen - Coordinate legal for marketplace terms and share indemnification language - Due 2027-05-11
[13:32] [00:13:32] Priya: Sounds good. Any outstanding blockers?
[13:36] Tomás: I'd like the resource estimates earlier so we can validate instance types with infra team.
[13:42] Maya: We'll prioritize the resource estimate snippet with the helm chart release.
[13:49] Evan: Minor: the marketplace requires an SLA section, what's Redwood's SLA for Dedicated?
[13:55] Alex: Redwood Dedicated SLA is 99.9% for availability; we'll share the specific SLA doc.
[14:03] Priya: Ok that should be fine.
[14:07] Alex: Any other questions?
[14:10] [00:14:10] Speaker 5 (customer): Uh, small note, sometimes the transcriptions mess up 'KV cache' as 'K V cache' in our docs, so watch for that in the RA.
[14:21] Samir: Ha, noted, we'll be careful.
[14:25] Alex: Great. We'll plan to reconvene after security deep-dive and after Redwood shares the artifacts. Target follow-up sync in two weeks.
[14:36] Priya: Two weeks works for me.
[14:39] Tomás: Works.
[14:41] Alex: Alright, thanks everyone. We'll send meeting notes and action items.
[14:46] [00:14:46] --- END TRANSCRIPT (partial; automated transcription may contain errors)
